correctness.rationale: Proof treats every dimension d>=3 and every path length n_i>=2. Minimum degree >=3 and at most two common neighbours provide the exclusive extension witnesses; N>2+2B outside Q3 provides the 00 witness for every pair. All vertices admit distance one, two, and three partners, giving the exact same pointed profile as C7. The three-quantifier domination sentence separates Q3. The minimal within-family nonexceptional order is 12. Two different finite checkers reproduce consequences, but the unbounded statement is proved analytically.

originality.rationale: The direct literature and available prior-claim comparisons did not find coverage for Cartesian products of three or more nontrivial paths at rank three, in particular the common equivalence with the odd seven-cycle. Previously established two-factor path-grid, hypercube, Hamming, and cycle-product results have strictly limited hypotheses and do not imply this assertion. A separately proved infinite-dimensional extension-pattern theorem is the new content. Complete historical priority remains unverified.
residual_risks: Search index is not exhaustive; a historical equivalent statement or a stronger general theorem could exist in unindexed finite-model-theory literature.

value.rationale: A complete two-class classification over arbitrary path-product dimension and arbitrary side lengths is a natural exact finite-model-theory invariant. The sharp eight/twelve order representatives and the unexpected equivalence between bipartite high-dimensional grids and the odd seven-cycle identify a concrete expressivity limitation beyond already-classified one- or two-dimensional grids and pure binary hypercubes.
